newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares extended Monday's gains in higher turnover but analysts said the stronger selling after price fixing signalled the market would lose steam on Wednesday and stay in a sideways trend.

"For a few weeks now we've had a horizontal trend -- after a few rises people sell and after falls they buy -- and it's hard to say which side will prevail," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said August's inflation figure and companies' August earnings results, both due next week, could provide the next signals to move the market in either direction.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.5 percent to 13,883.4 points and turnover rose 41.5 percent to 99.5 million zlotys ($35.8 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 58 to 11 with eight stocks stable.

Some analysts said mass privatisation NFI units, which rose 7.2 percent to 118 zlotys ($42.5) in record 49.5-million-zloty ($17.8 million) turnover, were drawing institutional capital from stocks, though others said such longer-term funds might soon transfer to shares.
In continuous trade, where no stocks saw action, the units rose 9.1 percent to 124 zlotys ($44.7) in 7.9-million-zloty ($2.8 million) trade.

Top gainer insurer Warta, up 8.1 percent, extended Monday's 9.9-percent surge after receiving 12.8 million zlotys ($4.6 million) in interest on overpaid taxes on Friday, but analysts said stronger post-price-fixing selling augured profit-taking.

They said most active steel trader Stalexport, up 1.9 percent in 13.7-million-zloty ($4.9 million) trade, should continue to see high turnovers before a court decision on Thursday on 75 million zlotys ($27 million0 in interest on overpaid taxes.
